# Results — Study 648 (Grain Seasonality): does corn/wheat/soy have a spring-high, harvest-low calendar? 2011–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly log returns of the three
Teucrium single-commodity grain ETFs — **CORN**, **WEAT**, **SOYB** — built from daily adjusted
closes resampled to month-end, plus the roll-naive **ZC=F / ZW=F / ZS=F** front-month futures
splice used only as a spot-price cross-check (never as something anyone could have earned).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; WEAT's 2011-09-19 inception sets the
common start). Fingerprints `81eafd725d20` (CORN) / `38378019b4f4` (WEAT) / `a1a9d64ef5f8`
(SOYB) / `1d148da3b3a1` (ZC=F) / `6b8a61301bbf` (ZW=F) / `c488e2ab74e4` (ZS=F).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes, CORN/WEAT/SOYB (Teucrium grain ETFs) and ZC=F/ZW=F/ZS=F (roll-naive front-month futures), 2011-10-03 → 2026-06-30, resampled to **176 month-end observations per series** |
| Agronomic calendar | **hardcoded** USDA NASS typical crop-progress windows per grain (planting / weather-scare / harvest) — facts, no network; see `GRAIN_CALENDAR` in [`grain_seasonality/data.py`](../grain_seasonality/data.py) |
| Statistics | one-sample naive + **Newey-West (HAC)** *t* per calendar month (36 cells, 3 grains × 12 months) with a **Bonferroni** bar for 36 simultaneous tests; Welch *t* for best/worst month vs rest and for spring-vs-harvest; a circular block-bootstrap CI (5,000 draws, 12-month blocks per grain) on the pooled spring-minus-harvest spread; Wilson interval on the seasonal timer's hit rate |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the calendar-known seasonal timer sets its position from the (fixed, published) USDA crop calendar alone — no signal-to-trade lag is needed. Round-trip costs: 4 one-way legs/yr × 10 bps × NAV, spread across the 12 months |
| Roll caveat (named) | CORN/WEAT/SOYB are **not** spot proxies — each ETF holds a weighted roll across near/second/third contract months and pays that roll's cost or benefit every month. ZC=F/ZW=F/ZS=F are a roll-naive front-month splice: **not tradable as a continuous series**, used only to size the ETF's own roll drag |

No survivorship on the Signal axis (single continuously-listed ETFs and continuous futures
tickers, not a cross-sectional panel).

## The headline — 3 grains × 12 months, Bonferroni-corrected

Bonferroni bar for 36 simultaneous tests (α = 0.05/36, df≈13): **|t| ≥ 4.05**.

| Grain | Best month | mean | Welch *t* (vs rest) | Worst month | mean | Welch *t* (vs rest) |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|
| CORN | Oct | **+1.37%** | +1.60 | Jul | −2.45% | −0.98 |
| WEAT | Oct | **+0.96%** | +1.80 | Aug | **−3.21%** | −1.68 |
| SOYB | Oct | **+1.26%** | +1.05 | Jul | −1.53% | −1.13 |

**Cells clearing the Bonferroni bar: 0/36.** No individual calendar month, for any grain, is a
certified anomaly. The largest *nominal* (uncorrected) one-sample HAC t-stats are WEAT-November
(t = −2.78), CORN-November (t = −2.45) and WEAT-August (t = −2.27) — none reach |t| = 4.05, and
all three are *negative* (bearish), the opposite sign from a "spring planting-scare high." The
best month for **every single grain** is October — inside the calendar's own harvest window, not
the spring weather-scare window the claim predicts.

## Spring (weather-scare) vs harvest, per grain — the "old-crop/new-crop" test

Each grain's own USDA-calendar weather-scare window vs its own harvest window (see the calendar
table above).

| Grain | Spring window | Spring mean | Harvest window | Harvest mean | Spread | Welch *t* |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CORN | Jun–Jul | −2.29% (n=29) | Sep–Nov | −0.38% (n=43) | **−1.92%** | −1.20 |
| WEAT | Mar–May | +0.20% (n=45) | Jun–Jul | −2.10% (n=29) | **+2.30%** | +1.13 |
| SOYB | Jul–Aug | −1.03% (n=28) | Sep–Nov | −0.02% (n=43) | **−1.01%** | −0.84 |

**Two of three grains point the wrong way.** For corn and soybeans the "weather-scare" window
actually under-performs the "harvest" window — the opposite of the folklore's sign. Only wheat
points the claimed direction, and it clears neither a nominal nor a Bonferroni bar (t = +1.13).

## Pooled spring vs harvest across all 3 grains (the decisive number)

| | Mean monthly return | n |
|---|---|--:|
| Spring (weather-scare, pooled) | −0.85% | 102 |
| Harvest (pooled) | −0.68% | 115 |
| **Spread** | **−0.17%** | — |
| **Welch *t*** | **−0.19** | — |
| **Block-bootstrap 95% CI** | **[−1.97%, +1.75%]** | 5,000 resamples, 12-month blocks/grain |

The pooled spread is a rounding error with a CI that straddles zero by roughly ten times its own
point estimate, and the *sign is even negative* — the average grain, pooled across all three
crops, is very slightly cheaper in the "scare" window than the "harvest" window. **No pooled
seasonal survives.**

## Third axis, part 1 — the ETF's own roll ("ETF contango" caveat)

Mean monthly return, ETF (the tradable, roll-costed instrument) vs the roll-naive front-month
futures splice (spot-price proxy, not tradable as a continuous series), one-sample *t* of the
monthly gap.

| Grain | ETF mean | Futures-splice mean | Drag (ETF − futures) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CORN | −53.8 bps/mo | −25.5 bps/mo | **−28.3 bps/mo** | −0.89 |
| WEAT | −94.8 bps/mo | −4.5 bps/mo | **−90.3 bps/mo** | **−5.09** |
| SOYB | +5.3 bps/mo | −4.4 bps/mo | +9.8 bps/mo | +0.45 |

WEAT's roll drag is large, **certified** (t = −5.09) — the ETF gives back **~1.08%/yr** relative
to its own roll-naive futures proxy, a cost paid every single month regardless of any calendar
view. Whatever week-to-week calendar edge existed in the futures curve, a WEAT holder pays away
most of it, unconditionally, to the mechanics of the weighted roll. Corn's drag is smaller and
not certified; soy's is even nominally positive (ETF beats the splice), a reminder that roll
drag is not a law of physics — it depends on the shape of each grain's own curve.

## Third axis, part 2 — the seasonal timer, gross/net, and does it beat a coin?

Long the spring window, short the harvest window, cash otherwise (calendar-known rule, no
execution lag); costs 4 one-way legs/yr × 10 bps × NAV.

| Grain | Buy&hold Sharpe (CAGR) | Timer gross Sharpe (CAGR) | Timer net Sharpe (CAGR) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CORN | −0.35 (−7.8%) | −0.25 (−4.3%) | −0.28 (−4.6%) |
| WEAT | −0.49 (−13.2%) | **+0.27** (+3.3%) | +0.25 (+2.9%) |
| SOYB | +0.04 (−0.8%) | −0.18 (−2.4%) | −0.22 (−2.8%) |
| **Equal-weight 3-grain** | −0.34 (−6.9%) | −0.03 (−0.5%) | −0.08 (−0.8%) |

WEAT's timer Sharpe flip looks dramatic, but it is a **de-levering artifact, not a discovered
edge**: the timer is flat (cash) for 5 of 12 months every year, which mechanically halves realized
vol on a structurally declining ETF (WEAT lost ~13%/yr buy-and-hold over this window) — it looks
better only because doing *less* of a bad trade is better than doing all of it, not because the
active legs earn anything. The direct test of "does the active leg earn anything" is the hit
rate:

| | Hit rate (active months only) | Wilson 95% | Mean per active month | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Pooled, all 3 grains** | **100/216 = 46.3%** | [39.8%, 53.0%] | −0.04 bps | **−0.09** |

**"Beats a coin?" — BUSTED.** The pooled seasonal timer's active-leg hit rate (46.3%) is
nominally *below* a coin flip and its Wilson interval straddles 50%; the mean active-month return
is indistinguishable from zero (t = −0.09). The Sharpe "improvement" over buy-and-hold comes
entirely from being in cash 5 months a year on an asset class that has lost money on average, not
from any predictive skill.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d. monthly-return world with a TUNABLE planted spring-premium /
harvest-discount pair; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (seasonal = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.36** (sd 1.02), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted seasonal = +6.0%/yr (seed 648) | **+5.64** |

The detector fires at roughly the nominal false-positive rate on the null (1/20, in line with
α ≈ 0.05) and lights up decisively on a planted spread. *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Pooled spring-vs-harvest spread **−0.17%/month, Welch *t* = −0.19**,
  block-bootstrap CI **[−1.97%, +1.75%]**. Zero of 36 (grain × month) cells clear the
  Bonferroni bar (|t| ≥ 4.05); two of three grains (corn, soy) even point the *wrong* direction
  from the claim; the best month for every grain is October, inside the calendar's own harvest
  window rather than the spring scare window. There is no certified month-of-year or
  season-of-year pattern on the real ETF tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even setting Signal aside, WEAT alone bleeds a **certified**
  −90.3 bps/month (t = −5.09) to its own roll relative to a roll-naive futures proxy — a cost
  larger than any of the study's own spring/harvest point estimates. The seasonal timer's
  Sharpe "improvement" is a de-leveraging artifact of sitting in cash half the year, not a
  discovered edge: its active-leg hit rate is 46.3% (Wilson [39.8%, 53.0%]) and its net Sharpe
  is still negative pooled (−0.08).
- **"Beats a coin?" — BUSTED.** The seasonal timer's active months hit 46.3% of the time
  (t = −0.09 on the mean) — no better than, and nominally worse than, a fair coin.
